name: Pfitzinger / Advanced Marathoning

citations.title: Faster Road Racing: 5K to Half Marathon

description: High-mileage, LT-anchored marathon system organized into four mesocycles. Built around medium-long runs (MLRs), lactate threshold runs of 4-7 miles at LT pace, and progressively long Sunday long runs. Plans available at 55, 70, and 85+ miles per week.
signature: Lactate threshold-anchored mesocycles with MLR (Medium-Long Run) and LT runs at 15K-HM race pace
philosophyNarrative: Pfitzinger's system is built for serious marathon runners and rests on three pillars: (1) high but progressive mileage — the more aerobic work you can absorb, the better you'll perform; (2) the lactate threshold is the single most important physiological marker for marathon — train it directly and often; (3) periodization through four mesocycles that systematically build endurance, then LT, then race-specific work, then taper. The signature workout is the LT run — typically 4-7 miles at lactate threshold pace (15K-HM race pace), preceded and followed by easy miles. The medium-long run (MLR) — a 12-15 mile run done mid-week — is what separates Pfitzinger from less aggressive marathon plans. It builds the cumulative aerobic load that prepares you for race day. Every plan culminates in race-specific tune-up races and a 3-week taper.

workouts.name: Recovery Run
workouts.shortDescription: Very easy recovery run between harder sessions

mainSet.cue: Slower than General Aerobic. The point is recovery — should leave you feeling better.

workouts.purpose: Promote recovery between hard sessions while maintaining aerobic work. Critical glue in high-mileage Pfitz plans.
cues: If you don't feel better at the end, you ran too hard
Pace is irrelevant — RPE is the gauge
Skip if genuinely fatigued

workouts.name: General Aerobic (GA)
workouts.shortDescription: Standard aerobic run at GA pace, the bulk of weekly mileage

mainSet.description: Steady run at General Aerobic pace
mainSet.cue: Conversational. Bulk of weekly mileage lives here — you'll do this 2-4× per week.

workouts.purpose: Aerobic development. Builds capillary density, mitochondrial function, and fatigue resistance. The 'glue' workout of Pfitzinger plans.
cues: Conversational pace — full sentences
Effort steady throughout
GA pace will feel slow at first; trust the system

workouts.name: Medium-Long Run (MLR)
workouts.shortDescription: Mid-week 12-15 mile run that separates Pfitzinger from less aggressive plans

mainSet.cue: Mid-week long run — typically Wednesday. Builds cumulative aerobic load that prepares you for race day.

workouts.purpose: Cumulative aerobic load. The MLR is what separates Pfitzinger from generic marathon plans — it doubles the aerobic stimulus by adding a mid-week long-ish effort.
cues: Endurance pace, not Marathon pace — controlled effort
Fuel mid-run on anything over 90 minutes
If you feel labored at GA pace, slow down

workouts.name: Long Run
workouts.shortDescription: Sunday long run, 16-22 miles depending on phase

mainSet.description: Long steady run at Endurance pace
mainSet.cue: The marquee endurance workout. Build to 18-22 miles by mid-program. Practice race-day fueling.

workouts.purpose: Develops the deep endurance base required to hold marathon pace for 26.2 miles. Pfitzinger's plans build to 20-22 mile peak long runs in advanced versions.
cues: Time on feet matters more than pace
Practice your race-day nutrition strategy
Effort steady, not rising

workouts.name: Long Run with Marathon-Pace Segment
workouts.shortDescription: Long run with embedded MP miles for race specificity

mainSet.description: Marathon-pace segment in middle of run
mainSet.cue: Lock into goal race pace. Should feel controlled, not strained.

workouts.purpose: Race-specific fatigue + pace tolerance. Used in race-prep mesocycle. Tests goal pace under accumulated fatigue.
cues: MP should feel sustainable — if labored, goal time is too aggressive
Practice race-day fueling during the run
Run final segment at planned race effort

workouts.name: Lactate Threshold Run (LT)
workouts.shortDescription: Pfitzinger's signature workout: 4-7 miles at LT pace within a longer run

mainSet.description: Continuous run at Lactate Threshold pace
mainSet.cue: 15K-HM race pace. Comfortably hard but sustainable for the duration. Should not be a fight.

workouts.purpose: Raises lactate threshold — the most important physiological adaptation for marathon. The 15K-HM pace is sustainable enough that you can do meaningful volume at it (4-7 miles) without overstressing.
cues: Should feel like 15K race pace, not 5K pace
If you can converse in full sentences, you're going too easy
If you can't speak more than a word, you're going too hard
Volume builds across the program: start at 4 miles, peak at 7 miles

workouts.name: VO2max Intervals
workouts.shortDescription: 600m-1600m reps at VO2max pace with jog recovery

mainSet.cue: 5K race pace. Reps should be even — first rep at the same pace as the last.

workouts.purpose: Develops VO2max and running economy. Used in race-prep mesocycle. Critical for shorter Pfitzinger plans (5K/HM) and useful in late marathon prep.
cues: First rep should feel almost too easy — pace stays the same throughout
If reps slow significantly, end the workout — don't grind
These workouts are non-negotiable in race-prep mesocycle

workouts.name: Tune-Up Race / Time Trial
workouts.shortDescription: 8K-15K race or simulated effort, used 3-5 weeks before goal race

mainSet.description: Race effort at race pace for the chosen distance
mainSet.cue: Race effort. Useful as VDOT/LT recalibration and race-day rehearsal.

workouts.purpose: Race-day rehearsal under real conditions. Recalibrates LT pace based on current fitness. Provides confidence and identifies pacing issues.
cues: Treat as a real race — proper warmup, race effort, cool down
Use the result to recalibrate LT pace for the rest of the program
Don't schedule within 2 weeks of goal race

workouts.name: Strides
workouts.shortDescription: 8-10× ~100m at faster than 5K pace, full recovery

mainSet.cue: Smooth and fast — not maximum sprint. Build to top speed gradually, hold for ~10 sec, decelerate.

workouts.purpose: Maintains neuromuscular sharpness and stride mechanics during heavy aerobic work. Tagged onto end of GA runs 1-2× per week.
cues: Quick turnover, not stride length
Should feel energizing, never depleting
Skip if very fatigued

phases.name: Mesocycle 1 — Endurance
phases.focus: Build aerobic base, accumulate mileage, introduce MLR. No threshold work yet.
phases.athleteNarrative: Welcome to Mesocycle 1 — Endurance. The goal here is mileage and aerobic base. Most weeks have a long run, a medium-long run (MLR), and several General Aerobic (GA) runs. The MLR is the workout that distinguishes this plan — a 12-15 mile mid-week effort that doubles your weekly aerobic stimulus. No threshold work yet — that comes next mesocycle. Trust the volume.

phases.name: Mesocycle 2 — Lactate Threshold + Endurance
phases.focus: Add LT work (4-7 mi at LT pace) while maintaining endurance. Long runs continue extending.
phases.athleteNarrative: Mesocycle 2 is the heart of Pfitzinger's system. The signature LT run enters: 4-7 miles at lactate threshold pace, sandwiched between warmup and cooldown. This is the single most important workout for marathon performance. MLRs and long runs continue. Mileage is at or near peak. Long runs occasionally include marathon-pace segments to start building race-pace tolerance under fatigue.

phases.name: Mesocycle 3 — Race Prep
phases.focus: Race-specific work: VO2max intervals, tune-up races, MP-segmented long runs. Mileage stays high.
phases.athleteNarrative: Mesocycle 3 sharpens you for race day. VO2max intervals (1000m reps at 5K pace) build the aerobic ceiling. Tune-up races recalibrate your LT pace under real conditions. Long runs include MP segments to dial in race-day pacing. This is the most demanding mesocycle — pay close attention to recovery and listen to your body.

phases.name: Mesocycle 4 — Taper
phases.focus: Reduce volume sharply while preserving intensity. Final tune-up race optional 10-14 days before.
phases.athleteNarrative: Mesocycle 4 — Taper. Volume drops to 70%, then 50%, then 35% of peak across the three weeks. Intensity is preserved (short LT efforts and strides) so you don't go flat. The work is done — sleep, eat, hydrate. Resist the urge to 'make up' missed training. Trust the program.

weeklyPatterns.notes: Endurance mesocycle. MLR Wednesday + long run Sunday creates the cumulative load. No quality work yet.
LT+Endurance: Tuesday LT run + Friday MLR + Sunday long run. The most demanding pattern — recovery between is critical.
5-day variant for time-limited runners. LT Tuesday, MLR Thursday, long run Sunday. Lower mileage but preserves Pfitzinger's structure.
Race-prep meso: V̇O₂, MLR, LT, and MP-segmented long run all in same week. Peak demand.
Recovery week — every 4th-5th week. MLR dropped, LT shortened, long run cut back.

taper.notes: Pfitzinger's 3-week taper: 75% / 55% / 40% volume. Intensity preserved via short LT efforts and strides. The work is done.

strengthRecommendation.philosophy: Pfitzinger and Douglas recommend 2× weekly strength sessions of 20-30 min focused on running-specific work: single-leg strength, core stability, hip mobility. Schedule on easy days, never adjacent to MLR or long run. Drop to maintenance during taper.

crossTrainingRecommendation.intensityGuidance: Cross-training is supplemental, not a replacement. Use only on rest days at GA-equivalent effort, max 30-45 min. Pfitzinger's plans assume running is the primary stimulus.

restrictions.rule: Designed for serious marathoners with established mileage base (35+ mpw). Not appropriate for first-time marathon or low-mileage runners.
restrictions.warningMessage: Pfitzinger's plans assume 35+ mpw base and serious marathon focus. For first marathons or lower mileage, Higdon's beginner/intermediate plans may be a better fit.

restrictions.rule: Built for the marathon (and the 5K-half marathon road races in Faster Road Racing). Not designed for ultras.
restrictions.warningMessage: Pfitzinger's system is optimized for road races up to the marathon. For ultras, consider Koop or Roche.

restrictions.rule: Plans assume 6 days/week running availability with daily flexibility for MLR (12-15 mi mid-week). Hard for runners with rigid weekday constraints.
restrictions.warningMessage: Pfitzinger requires 6 days/week and a mid-week 12-15 mile run. If you can't run 6 days or do a 90+ minute weekday run, consider a 4-5 day plan like Higdon Intermediate.

invariants: Long run must not exceed 30% of weekly mileage
MLR (Wed/Thu) must not be on consecutive day with LT or long run
Minimum 2 days between any two hard sessions
LT volume builds: 4 mi → 5 mi → 6 mi → 7 mi across mesocycle 2
Cutback every 4-5 weeks at 75% of prior week
If user's currentWeeklyMileage < 35, recommend lower-mileage variant or alternative method
Tune-up race scheduled 3-5 weeks before goal race in race-prep mesocycle
